brief: Deutsche Bank's daily macro wrap. Dovish comments from Fed Governor Waller, who cast doubt on a hike this month and said recent data show signs of disinflation, drove a cross-asset rally and cut futures-implied odds of a September hike to 51% from 63% at Wednesday's close. That, plus European natural gas falling 2.48% after a near 10% three-day rise, paused the global bond selloff. Equities benefited more than US long-end bonds: the S&P 500 rose 1.06%, its best day in almost a month, while the 10yr Treasury yield fell only 1.1bps to 4.77% and the 2yr fell 3.2bps to 4.34%, which the note reads as Fed commentary driving the move. Yesterday's US data leant hawkish and offset Waller: ISM services hit a 6-month high of 55.4 and prices paid a 4-year high of 72.6, a series the note says correlates with inflation at a 3-month lag. Focus shifts to today's August jobs report, where DB economists forecast payrolls rebounding +65k after July's contraction with unemployment steady at 4.1%. In Japan, household spending fell 3.6% year-on-year, an eighth straight monthly contraction, ahead of a BoJ meeting Bloomberg reports is leaning toward a 25bp hike.
